newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Crew error caused latest major Mir problem.
newsitem.headline: Crew error caused latest major Mir problem.

text.p: One of the cosmonauts aboard the Mir space station mistakenly pulled out a vital cable that led to the massive power failure aboard the crippled ship on Thursday, mission director Vladimir Solovyov said.

"I should stress it is an especially unpleasant situation," Solovyov told reporters. He would not say who, of the two Russians and one American aboard, was responsible. The crewman immediately replaced the cable but the damage was done, he said, forcing the crew to shut down all systems in the main section.

"This was purely human error," Solovyov said. "They honestly acknowledged they detached this cable. Now they are grappling with this." It was not clear exactly what sort of cable was involved but it appeared to be linked to computer systems.

Solovyov said the crew, whose commander encountered heart problems this week, had been told to continue with preparations for a risky operation in spacesuits next week to repair electric cables severed after a collision on June 25.

But with no artificial light, the crew must rely on daylight available for about half of every two-hour orbit of the Earth. Mission Control officials have declined to confirm or deny reports that a mistake by the commander caused the original accident, which was the worst in Mir's 11 years in space.

Solovyov said there were no plans to abandon ship. Mir can tolerate the loss of temperature control for two to three days. Communications with Earth were being routed through a Progress spacecraft moored on Mir while the station's systems were down.
